To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FilGAP and close relatives are key mediators of Rho-RAC antagonism that regulate cell morphology, migration and the amoeboid-mesenchymal transition.
FilGAP, ARHGAP22 and ARHGAP25 are GAPs for Rac1 and are involved in Rho-Rac signalling that regulates cell morphology, migration and the mesenchyme-amoeboid mode transition.

FilGAP and ARHGAP22 act as mediators of RhoA-Rac1 antagonism that regulate actin assembly and cell shape changes, and that they are key regulators that control the mesenchymalm-amoeboid cell migration transition in tumour progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of FilGAP and other ARHGAPs in cell shape changes and cell motility.
the molecular mechanisms that control the dynamic regulation of the actin and Rho family GTPase networks in cells.
the molecular mechanisms of the mechanical regulation of the actin-based cytoskeleton, and the role of the FilGAP family proteins in cell shape changes and cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FilGAP and close relatives are a mediator of RAC-Rho antagonism that regulates the actin cyto-skeleton and cell morphology and migration.
FilGAP is an important mediator of RhoA and RhoA-activated ROCK, which regulates Rac1 to control actin assembly, cell morphology and cell movement.
the Rho-Rac1 antagonism is mediated by FilGAP and related GAPs to regulate cell morphology and migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FilGAP is an actomyosin-regulated RhoA-Rac1 mediator that controls actin assembly and cell migration.
FilGAP is an F-actin-cross-linking protein that acts as a mediator of the antagonistic relationship between Rho and Rac GTPases in the regulation of cell morphology and motility.
FilGAP, ARHGAP22 and ARHGAP25 act as mediators of the antagonistic Rho-Rac signalling pathway, which regulates cell morphology, cell motility and cell migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FilGAP and other ARHGAPs are important regulators of the actomyosin system that controls cell shape changes and motility.
FilGAP and FLNa are important regulators of cell morphology and migration that are controlled by mechanical forces. © 2014 Biochemical Society.
